hints.title: Two Distinct Types Subarray Squeeze Obstacle
hints.text: Checking all possible orchard slices takes quadratic time. Because you may pick from at most two distinct varieties, how can you slide an observation window across the trees and shrink the back edge whenever a third fruit variety appears?

hints.title: Bounded Diversity Window Invariant
hints.text: Maintain frequency counts of fruits in the current slice. Expand the front marker to gather fruit; whenever the count of unique keys exceeds two, increment the back marker and reduce counts until diversity is at most two.

hints.title: Sliding Window Diversity Contraction Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left to zero, max_fruits to zero, and an empty frequency table. Iterate right through the tree array, incrementing counts for fruits[right]. While the number of unique keys exceeds two, decrement the count for fruits[left], remove it if its count hits zero, and increment left. Update max_fruits with the window width right minus left plus one. Return max_fruits.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of fruits array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Dynamic sliding window with at most 2 distinct keys; frequency table size <= 3.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every starting tree and walking until 3 varieties are seen takes O(N^2) time, hitting Time Limit Exceeded on N=10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since each tree index is added and removed at most once, the dynamic window runs in linear O(N) time with O(1) space (at most 3 keys).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that this problem is isomorphic to longest contiguous subarray with at most two distinct elements.
